column13:
Please give sincere consideration to the transportation needs of Evening & Weekend students, many of whom rely on parking to access the Berkeley campus. Unlike most full-time or undergraduate students, the vast majority of EW students commute 30 minutes or more after a full workday. In addition to the significant time commitment, many already incur substantial commuting costs, including gas and Bay Bridge tolls.

The removal of complimentary parking creates an additional financial burden for a population that is balancing demanding careers, academics, and personal responsibilities. Maintaining affordable parking options would meaningfully improve accessibility and help ensure that Evening & Weekend students can continue to fully participate in the Berkeley community.

EWMBA students primarily live far from campus and typically have to drive. Excluding a parking permit from enrollment while requiring students to pay an additional $125 per month for a parking pass, and justifying this by saying it aligns with other MBA programs, creates the impression that EWMBA students are being treated as second-class members of the Haas community and as a source of additional revenue.

If the program were to waive the other campus fees that EWMBA students rarely benefit from, allowing students to opt in only if they choose to use those facilities, then it would be reasonable for parking to be treated as an optional benefit as well. However, requiring EWMBA students to pay mandatory fees for amenities that most of them seldom use, and then charging extra for parking on top of those fees, is difficult to justify.

FTMBA students live closer to campus and spend the majority of their day in classes and campus activities, such as recruiting. Evening students must commute after their workday, and live scattered across the Bay Area (and in some cases, beyond). Many of these students rely on their cars for the commute, and also have less predictability in schedules, making the option for a car invaluable. Given this, it clearly does not make sense to align these two programs on an issue such as parking. I’m sure I’ll end up paying for a permit, but it does give the program more of a transactional feel to it, and I don’t believe I’m alone in that sentiment.

column13:
The spectrum of transit options is now too wide and no longer equitable. I work full-time; my job is in Marin while I live in San Francisco. It does not feel fair or reasonable to know that someone gets a free ride to/from the South Bay, I have to pay for a Bay Pass that I do not even have the option to use, and I now have to pay to park on campus (in addition to very expensive gas and bridge tolls, while putting mileage on my own car). 

If I was a full-time student, I would choose to live in Berkeley, but that is not a reasonable option given my work location. I understand that we are trying to reduce cars on campus and am fully supportive of that, but it's simply not a reasonable option for me as a full-time employee of an org based in Marin. I seriously considered the Flex student route to avoid all of this. There are already so many restrictions to maximizing an MBA experience as a part-time student (/full-time employee) and I really hope that parking affordability isn't added to the list. I've always carpooled when possible. Please reconsider this landscape for part-time MBAs.

Do not let the relative magnitude of this cost compared to the cost of tuition reduce the significance of this change for students. This is another drop in what has become a noticeably full bucket of value reduction. The particularly hurtful part for many students is clearly that this policy decision was made in the name of equity with the other MBA programs. EW students CONSISTENTLY feel that the full time students receive preferential treatment compared to the EW students, who earn the same degree. This includes CMG access, club access, scholarship availability and size, and campus resources (eg ability to book classrooms, unless I’m mistaken). Program office, please use our responses to push back against those in admin who do not understand that they are threatening the reputation of Haas and Berkeley at large by thinking that Haas’ budget allocations are zero-sum. That their impact stops at “our program or your program”. The issue is not about parking, it’s about concession after concession forced onto the EW program in what appears to be a tone deaf and ivory tower negotiation with the other MBA program decision makers, who somehow always manage to “win”. 

Haas and Berkeley continue to lose while these people win.

column13:
As an EWMBA student, I am charged a number of mandatory student fees for services that provide little to no practical value to me. For example, I am unable to make use of the gymnasium or student recreational facilities. My time on campus is limited to Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and I commute from San Jose while balancing a full-time job and caring for an infant. Realistically, I have neither the time nor the opportunity to take advantage of many of the services these fees support.

One could argue that nothing technically prevents me from using these facilities. However, the reality of the EWMBA program is that students like me have significantly different schedules and commitments than full-time students. While I recognize that these fees are part of my obligations as a student and have always paid them without objection, I accepted those obligations with the understanding of the policies that were in place when I enrolled.

What is particularly disappointing is having the terms effectively change after I have already invested substantial time, effort, and financial resources into the program. It feels like a bait-and-switch—joining under one set of expectations only to have those expectations altered once it is no longer practical to reconsider the decision. That has had a genuinely demoralizing effect and has left me feeling that the unique circumstances of EWMBA students are not being adequately considered.

1. When we applied for and accepted the offer into Haas EWMBA, the website says it will provide either (1) free parking permit or (2) shuttle that students can "choose" to minimize the inconvenience of commuting to school after works, and now it suddenly just announced things going to change in the middle of the program. Not sure if there are any reasons to justify.

2. Announcement was made suddenly about a month before fall semester start without any proper communications/townhall with students. How people can react to these changes?

3. Not sure how many MBA programs are there at Haas. Aren't there just full-time, part-time, and executive? EWMBA students have full-time jobs unlike full-time MBA and have a much longer semester compared with EMBA. How can a statement "aligned with other MBA programs at Haas" justify this action? Isn't that true this action just want to extract more profits from whoever already paid the sunk cost and cannot get away?

4. Cancelling permits all at once are too aggressive, aren't they? Why not letting weekday cohorts have weekday evening permit (e.g. after 5 PM only) and weekend cohorts have Saturday permit (e.g. after 8 AM until 6 PM) so that at least students can still have the rights during their "class time". All the electives can just use codes or something.
